content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be easier or different for you compared with how you handle bookmarks today?

Honestly, the main thing is I want to stop losing links. Right now I paste things into notes and emails to myself and I can never find them again.

So when this is done, I'd love to just drop in a web address and have it saved — and ideally it figures out the page's title and a little description on its own, so I'm not typing all that in. Then later I want to actually *find* things: search by words, and organize with tags or labels so I can pull up, say, everything about cooking in one click.

A couple of other things that matter to me: some links I save meaning to read later, so I'd want a way to set those aside and come back to them. And if I save something I've already saved, I don't want a bunch of duplicates piling up — it should just take me to the one I already have.

That's the gist of my frustration today. Where would you like to start?

content: If a webpage later changes its title or description—or disappears entirely—what should happen to the title, description, note, and labels already saved in Trove?

What I've saved in Trove is mine, so it should just stay put. Once I've saved a link — especially after I've tweaked the title or description, written a note, and put labels on it — none of that should quietly change or vanish because the website did something on their end.

So if the page later changes its title or description, I wouldn't want Trove to silently overwrite what I saved with the new version; my copy stays as I left it. And if the page disappears entirely, everything I kept — the title, description, my note, and my labels — should still be right there in my collection. The whole reason I'm saving these is so I don't lose them, so a link going bad on the web shouldn't take my saved details down with it.

The real app is ready at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

All 16 approved behaviors passed verification, including 10 storage/API tests and the complete Chromium browser flow. The app starts with an empty, persistent personal collection.

Please try it as a whole, beginning by pasting a web address. If it matches the behavior we approved, do you accept the software and agree to complete this cycle?

I sat down and actually put it through its paces, and it does what we agreed on. I dropped in a link and it saved with the title, description, labels, and a read-later flag; when I pasted the very same address again — even with a trailing slash and a "?ref=" tacked on — it recognized my existing bookmark instead of making a duplicate, and kept my edits. Search found things by the title, by a word in my note, and by part of the web address, and it didn't care about capitals; a word that matched nothing gave me the calm "nothing matches" rather than losing my collection. My Read later list showed only what I'd set aside, and marking something done dropped it off there while keeping it saved. Labels behaved too — filtering to a topic worked, and typing a label with odd spacing or capitals folded into the one I already had instead of splitting it. And it starts empty and holds onto what I save.

That's the app I asked for, and it matches everything we approved together. I'm happy to accept it and complete this cycle.

For somewhere down the road — no change needed now — I'd still love to eventually get to a couple of things we didn't take up this time, like tidying away links I'm done with without deleting them, and a keepsake copy of a page in case it vanishes. Just noting those for a future round; they don't hold up my acceptance today.
